During a military-family move, Marketa keeps a clearly marked first-night box within reach so temporary quarters can function before full unpacking.
Candidate scene: bedding, toiletries, a lamp, and one familiar comfort object are separated from the larger shipment. Marketa treats preparation as ordinary care and does not promise that the move will feel easy.
people: Embry Lawson, Marketa Lawson; concepts: portable home
Setting: age band 04-10. Situation: During a military-family move, Marketa keeps a clearly marked first-night box within reach so temporary quarters can function before full unpacking. Trigger: Marketa opens the first-night box before decorative boxes. Stakes: Embry looks for organized rituals when places change.
Emotions: relief. Intensity: 2/5. Regulation: family ritual and portable anchors. Conflict: 
Theory of mind: relationship: Embry begins to associate Marketa with continuity that can be packed and reopened. Trigger: Marketa opens the first-night box before decorative boxes. Consequence: Embry looks for organized rituals when places change.

Before another move, Marketa gives Embry a picture card with three categories: carry, open first, and later.
Candidate scene: Marketa converts a large transition into manageable steps. Embry marks progress without being asked to predict when she will feel settled.
people: Embry Lawson, Marketa Lawson; objects: OPEN FIRST box, POINT/PATH/PEOPLE checklist; concepts: Precision
Setting: age band 04-10. Situation: Before another move, Marketa gives Embry a picture card with three categories: carry, open first, and later. Trigger: Rooms become partially packed and hard to read. Stakes: Visible categories strengthen her reliance on procedures and completion checks.
Emotions: uncertainty. Intensity: 2/5. Regulation: procedural verification. Conflict: 
Theory of mind: goal: Embry wants uncertainty divided into steps she can complete. Trigger: Rooms become partially packed and hard to read. Consequence: Visible categories strengthen her reliance on procedures and completion checks.

Marketa lets Embry count and place labels on the boxes designated to open first.
Candidate scene: Embry receives a small, bounded job rather than adult responsibility for the move. Counting labels turns waiting into participation.
people: Embry Lawson, Marketa Lawson; objects: OPEN FIRST box, POINT/PATH/PEOPLE checklist; concepts: portable home, Precision
Setting: age band 04-10. Situation: Marketa lets Embry count and place labels on the boxes designated to open first. Trigger: Marketa assigns a concrete labeling task. Stakes: Participation lowers helplessness and seeds later checklist behavior.
Emotions: uncertainty. Intensity: 2/5. Regulation: procedural verification. Conflict: 
Theory of mind: goal: Embry wants a useful role in making the next home ready. Trigger: Marketa assigns a concrete labeling task. Consequence: Participation lowers helplessness and seeds later checklist behavior.
